title: Chemical Equilibrium
seo_title: Equilibrium Worksheets: Le Chatelier's Principle and the Haber Process (High School Chemistry)
standard_text: Refine the design of a chemical system by specifying a change in conditions that would produce increased amounts of products at equilibrium.
meta_desc: Free high school chemistry worksheets on chemical equilibrium (NGSS HS-PS1-6): reversible reactions, dynamic equilibrium and Le Chatelier's principle for concentration, temperature and pressure. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Change one condition and the system shifts to reduce the change.
body_html:
How to think about it

At equilibrium, forward and reverse rates are equal.

  • Amounts stay constant but are usually not equal. The reaction keeps going both ways.
  • Le Chatelier: add reactant or remove product → shift right. Heat favors the endothermic direction. Higher pressure favors fewer gas moles.
  • A catalyst speeds up both directions; it does not change how much product forms.
Example

N2 + 3H2 ⇌ 2NH3, ΔH = −92 kJ. Heat it?

Forward is exothermic

Heat favors endothermic (left)

Answer: shifts left

Example

Same reaction, raise pressure?

4 gas moles → 2 gas moles

Answer: shifts right

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the reaction stops at equilibrium.
  • Thinking amounts are equal at equilibrium.
  • Thinking a catalyst makes more product.

faq.a: A state in a closed system where the forward and reverse reactions happen at the same rate, so the amounts stay constant.

faq.q: How do you get more product at equilibrium?
faq.a: Add reactant, remove product, change the temperature toward the side that favors products, or change the pressure for gas reactions.
No. It speeds up the forward and reverse reactions equally, so the system reaches equilibrium faster but the amounts do not change.

items.q: In making ammonia (Haber process): N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2NH<sub>3</sub>, ΔH = −92 kJ. The temperature is lowered. How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: ΔH = −92 kJ, so the forward reaction is exothermic. Cooling favors the exothermic direction.

items.q: In making sulfuric acid (contact process): 2SO<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2SO<sub>3</sub>, ΔH = −198 kJ. The temperature is raised. How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: ΔH = −198 kJ, so the forward reaction is exothermic. Heating favors the endothermic direction.

items.q: What is a reversible reaction?
c: a reaction that can go forward and backward
a reaction that only goes forward
items.e: Symbol ⇌.

items.q: In making ammonia (Haber process): N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2NH<sub>3</sub>, ΔH = −92 kJ. Some N<sub>2</sub> is removed. How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: The system shifts to use up what was added or replace what was removed.

items.q: What is true at chemical equilibrium?
c: The forward and reverse reactions happen at the same rate.
Reactants and products are always equal in amount.
items.e: Dynamic equilibrium.

c: At low temperature the reaction is too slow; 450 °C is a compromise between rate and yield.
items.e: Rate vs yield.

items.q: Why does the Haber process use high pressure (about 200 atm)?
c: 4 mol of gas form 2 mol, so high pressure shifts toward ammonia.
To speed up the catalyst only.
items.e: Fewer gas moles.

items.q: In a closed flask of PCl₅: PCl<sub>5</sub> ⇌ PCl<sub>3</sub> + Cl<sub>2</sub>, ΔH = +88 kJ. The pressure is decreased (the container is made larger). How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: Left: 1 mol gas, right: 2 mol gas. Higher pressure favors fewer gas moles; lower pressure favors more.

items.q: Factories remove ammonia as it forms. Why?
c: Removing product shifts the equilibrium to make more ammonia.
items.e: Le Chatelier.

items.q: In making ammonia (Haber process): N<sub>2</sub> + 3H<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2NH<sub>3</sub>, ΔH = −92 kJ. The pressure is decreased (the container is made larger). How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: Left: 4 mol gas, right: 2 mol gas. Higher pressure favors fewer gas moles; lower pressure favors more.

items.q: A student says equilibrium means 50% reactants and 50% products. What is correct?
c: Equilibrium means constant amounts and equal rates, not equal amounts.
items.e: Common misconception.

items.q: In making sulfuric acid (contact process): 2SO<sub>2</sub> + O<sub>2</sub> ⇌ 2SO<sub>3</sub>, ΔH = −198 kJ. Some O<sub>2</sub> is removed. How does the equilibrium respond?
items.e: The system shifts to use up what was added or replace what was removed.
